Rotate the upper assembly so that the 22mm machined wrench can fit on the shaft -turn the machined side toward the actuation cylinder. <<nl/>><<nl/>>2. Place the modified 25mm wrench on the large, polished, facet headed bellows screw, the screw breaks with a righthand turn with you facing the bottom of the assembly. <<nl/>><<nl/>>3. Once the screw is loose, things go quicker if the assembly is removed from the vise, turned upside down so that the bellows sit on the table and the actuation cylinder rotated while the bellows is kept still - the nut should finally free and the seal plate and actuation cylinder should separate. <<nl/>><<nl/>>NOTE: Note: The Manufacturer uses lock tight on this part and it may be very difficult to move initially. Heat to < 250 Celsius if necessary to loosen 12 sided nut.

record.field:
Disassemble
1. Rotate the upper assembly so that the 22mm machined wrench can fit on the shaft -turn the machined side toward the actuation cylinder.
2. Place the modified 25mm wrench on the large, polished, facet headed bellows screw, the screw breaks with a righthand turn with you facing the bottom of the assembly.
3. Completely loosen the bellow screw. The screw has fine threads so this takes about 15 minutes. Once the screw is loose, things go quicker if the assembly is removed from the vise, turned upside down so that the bellows sit on the table and the actuation cylinder rotated while the bellows is kept still - the nut should finally free and the seal plate and actuation cylinder should separate.
NOTE: Note: The Manufacturer uses lock tight on this part and it may be very difficult to move initially. Rock the 25mm wrench to the right while keeping the 22mm wrench on the actuation cylinder shaft - this motion will slowly loosen excessively tight screws. Some cylinders will not allow the bellow nut to be loosened while the cylinder is rotated, these cases will require that the part be kept in the vise and the screw is loosened totally using the 25mm and 22mm wrenches. Heat to < 250 Celsius if necessary to loosen 12 sided nut.

3. Completely loosen the bellow screw. The screw has fine threads so this takes about 15 minutes. Once the screw is loose, things go quicker if the assembly is removed from the vise, turned upside down so that the bellows sit on the table and the actuation cylinder rotated while the bellows is kept still - the nut should finally free and the seal plate and actuation cylinder should separate.

record.field:
Disassemble
1. Clean the actuation cylinder assembly by wiping the body down, (3) times with IPA dampened wipe.
2. Remove the residual lock tight and oil from the bellows screw hole of the cylinder. It helps to use an o-ring pick inside of an IPA dampened wipe when trying to remove the lock tight and oil.
3. Examine the cylinder for signs of excessive wear - the cylinder can be purchased from new from SMC, Inc or rebuilt.
4. Insure that the part is cleaned of all visible oil.
Once the part is clean and inspected, put it on the clean parts section of the bench and change clean gloves. MSR will use a 5/8-18 tap and die to remove the excess Loctite from the threads

div.root:

3. Examine the cylinder for signs of excessive wear - the cylinder can be purchased from new from SMC, Inc or rebuilt.
4. Insure that the part is cleaned of all visible oil.
Once the part is clean and inspected, put it on the clean parts section of the bench and change clean gloves. MSR will use a 5/8-18 tap and die to remove the excess Loctite from the threads

record.field:
Disassemble
1. Remove the 1/8th shoulder screw that retains the bellows screw on the end of the bellows shaft. The bellows screw will slip off the shaft.
2. Clean the bellows screw, remove as much lock tight as possible.
3. Remove ALL oil - this part has oil all over. Clean it patiently to remove all oil. Oil will exist inside and outside this part and in it''s threads.
4. Clean the shoulder screw, remove all oil from it - it too has oil all over.
Place the clean bellows screw and shoulder screw onto the clean part of the workbench.

record.field:
Disassemble
1. Double glove. Clean the buffer sealplate.
2.This clean is best done by wiping the entire plate down with Acetone dampened wipes (3x) times.
3. If acetone is not available or cannot be used use IPA, but increase the number of wipedowns to 6x.
4. Carefully squirt a small amount of IPA into openings and crevices to remove hidden oil.
5. Change gloves. Wipe the part down with IPA dampened wipes (3x) times.
6. Place it on the clean side of the workbench with other oil-free parts.
NOTE: The buffer sealplate damages easily on the anodized side that sits on the vacuum side. Always protect this part to prevent damage to it by other parts of the actuator. It is advised that this part get extra packaging if it is being transported.

div.root:

5. Change gloves. Wipe the part down with IPA dampened wipes (3x) times.
6. Place it on the clean side of the workbench with other oil-free parts.

record.field:
Disassemble
Cleaning of the Actuator Bellows
1. To clean the bellows, remove the 3/32nd screw that is at the top of the cover.
2. The screw is silver-plated, replace with a stainless steel screw - the washers can be replaced or cleaned and reused.
3. Place the bellow cover aside to be cleaned later.
4. Carefully clean the new screw with IPA.
5. Remove the o-ring that seals the buffer chamber.
6. Change gloves.
7. Clean a new o-ring with IPA, place it on the clean side with other cleaned, oil-free parts.
8. Change gloves again and double glove.
7. Remove bellows lower skirt to clean pleats.
The stainless screw size can be found in the fab breadman - retain the washers, they are hard to locate. Insure that the old screw is used to select the replacement and that the washers and new screw are cleaned with IPA.Bellows seal o-ring material and size: Brown Viton 1.484 ID x 0.139 cx. CSF part# 333-221V884-75.

div.root:

7. Clean a new o-ring with IPA, place it on the clean side with other cleaned, oil-free parts.
8. Change gloves again and double glove.
7. Remove bellows lower skirt to clean pleats.

field.value: <<bb>>Wipe <</bb>> <<nl/>><<nl/>>Wiper Material: Woven Polyester <<nl/>>Wiper Class: Class 100 <<nl/>>Solvent: Isopropyl Alchohol <<nl/>>Concentration: 1<<nl/>><<nl/>>1. Clean the bellows cover (6x) times with IPA dampened wipes. Insure the wipes are damp, but not saturated. <<nl/>><<nl/>>2. Once the outside of the bellows has been wipes and most of the oil removed, change into a clean pair of gloves.<<nl/>><<nl/>>3. Dampen a wipe with IPA. Use a clean Allen key to gently pack the wipe into the bellows housing. <<nl/>><<nl/>>4. Leave enough of the wipe outside the housing to allow you to rotate the wipe around the shaft while keeping it packed in the housing.<<nl/>><<nl/>>5. Remove the wipe after 4 rotations around the shaft. The wipe should have picked up oil.<<nl/>><<nl/>>6. Repeat Steps 3-5 until no oil can be collected from the bellows housing.<<nl/>><<nl/>>7. Once the condition of Step 7 is met, dampen a clean wipe with IPA. Use a small Allen key to work the wipe into holes for screws and two alignment pin holes. DO NOT use a sharp pointed object like a screwdriver, an Allen key works.<<nl/>><<nl/>>8. Repeat Step 7 until no oil is picked up from the holes.<<nl/>><<nl/>>9. 1. Clean the bellows cover (6x) times with IPA dampened wipes. Insure the wipes are damp, but not saturated.
2. Once the outside of the bellows has been wipes and most of the oil removed, change into a clean pair of gloves.
3. Dampen a wipe with IPA. Use a clean Allen key to gently pack the wipe into the bellows housing.
4. Leave enough of the wipe outside the housing to allow you to rotate the wipe around the shaft while keeping it packed in the housing.
5. Remove the wipe after 4 rotations around the shaft. The wipe should have picked up oil.
6. Repeat Steps 3-5 until no oil can be collected from the bellows housing.
7. Once the condition of Step 7 is met, dampen a clean wipe with IPA. Use a small Allen key to work the wipe into holes for screws and two alignment pin holes. DO NOT use a sharp pointed object like a screwdriver, an Allen key works.
8. Repeat Step 7 until no oil is picked up from the holes.
9. Use an IPA dampened wipe to clean out the o-ring groove on the bellows. Repeat the procedure until all oil is removed from the o-ring groove.
10. Once no more oil can be found anywhere on the bellows, change gloves.
11. Wipe down the entire bellows using and IPA dampened wipe.
12. Use an N2 gun to blow dry all parts of the bellows. If an N2 gun is not available allow the bellows to air dry for at least 2 hours.
13. It is very important that no residual IPA gets left in the bellows housing and that the bellows is completely free of oil, if these conditions are not met repeat Steps 1-12 until they are.

1. To tighten use the machined 22mm wrench and the 25mm wrench.
2. Insure that the wrenches are wiped first to remove any oil that may have gotten on them when the dirty actuator was disassembled.
3. The position of the wrenches is the same that was used for disassembly.

6. Tighten the bellows screw until it is firmly tight (no rotation in response to attempts to tighten more).
7. Avoid forcing to the point where the 25mm wrench slips over the screw head.
